findings.text: follow-on: a lift that leaves force by disappearing from the document rather than by a clear stamp, an end time, the ceiling or an ended lift is re-announced as lift-granted, not lift-ended. In the ended loop a lift in seen that is no longer in force computes cause = end_cause(...); when the lift is still within its window and unreset the cause is None, and _lift_row keys current on `ended is not None`, so a None cause falls through to the LIFT_GRANTED branch and the follower announces a fresh grant for a lift that has stopped. Reproduced: grant a lift, sweep, remove it from budget-lifts.json while it remains in its window, sweep again -- the third row is `lift-granted` with no cause, where the contract is one row when a lift leaves, naming what ended it. Lower severity because the document retains ended lifts as history, so this is reachable only when budget-lifts.json is reset while a lift is live.

follow-on: test_the_rows_render_through_both_followers still asserts only isinstance(format_watch_transition(row), str) and isinstance(Ticker().render(row), str), which pass for any rendering that does not raise; the dedicated rendered-clause cases at :184 and :295 carry the strong assertion, so this is the weak residue of the predecessor review's same finding, and it cannot redden on a ticker that drops the clause.

follow-on: _end_moment still dispatches on ends.kind beside the new public end_cause (:649), so two functions read the same two shapes of ends to answer the end question -- one the instant for the budget view's ends_at/ends_on, the other the cause for the watch row; end_cause replaced _end_moment on the in-force path but _end_moment survives for _lift_summary, and a future end kind must be added to both.

follow-on: the reviewed manifest's changed_paths names tests/test_budget_lift.py, and both arms' recorded commands carry literal `<66 files>`/`<67 files>` placeholders with no log_path in the suite JSON; the diff carries no change to tests/test_budget_lift.py, and because the suite fields name no gate log a reader's read-time added-failure annotation resolves unmeasured for this run even though the two logs (base-suite.log, head-suite.log) exist and show zero added failures.
